source.title: Critical Damping as a Momentum Schedule: Multi-Seed Validation, a Hybrid Recipe, and an Exhaustive Negative Result on Surgical Layer Selection

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Its own results refine the optimizer-related generalization claim: on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, the tested momentum schedule reaches an early accuracy threshold faster but has lower final test accuracy; a hybrid schedule recovers the final-accuracy difference. The paper also reports a distinct exhaustive layer-selection result outside the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests momentum schedules and reports test accuracy, which bears on V4. Its layer-attribution and surgical-correction experiments concern layer selection and correction outcomes; those do not test any listed version about training/test generalization gaps. Cited optimizer comparisons are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: Section 7.2 directly compares Adam with momentum SGD using test accuracy after training ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10. This tests V4, although only for one seed and fixed optimizer settings. The extracted momentum-schedule comparisons do not themselves test adaptive versus nonadaptive optimization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the schedule findings: faster intermediate convergence carries a systematic best-accuracy deficit, and Hybrid-90 recovers baseline-like accuracy on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10. It omits the other principal conclusion: exhaustive testing overturns the claimed optimal layer-selection benefit, leaving weaker top-layer and harm-avoidance signals.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a momentum schedule derived from an oscillator model, rather than the original studies' natural-label generalization or train/test-error-gap interventions. It does not test the listed claim's memorization setup or measure a training/test error gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported speed and final test accuracy vary by schedule, architecture, dataset, accuracy threshold, and hybrid switch rule. On CIFAR-100, the milestone choice changes the reported speed comparison; Hybrid-ep52 fails to retain the early advantage seen with Hybrid-90.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical-damping SGD momentum reaches intermediate test-accuracy thresholds faster but has lower best accuracy; an accuracy-triggered SGD hybrid recovers baseline-like best accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global momentum scheduling can trade intermediate convergence speed against best test accuracy, with outcomes depending on architecture, dataset, threshold, and switching rule.

fits_no_version.finding: The gradient-selected repair triple ranks 11th among 35 combinations; combinations containing the highest-ranked layer average better outcomes, while several low-ranked combinations are harmful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Error-gradient layer rankings provide limited repair guidance and require combinatorial selection controls.

record.problems: Core schedule claims use five seeds; architecture and dataset arms use three seeds. The paper says runs are not bit-deterministic and describes p-values as descriptive rather than confirmatory. Results cover CIFAR-scale image classification with SGD and momentum; hybrid validation on CIFAR-100 and transfer to VGG are untested.
record.rows_left_out: The layer attribution and surgical correction results in Sections 6–8 do not measure a listed version's named generalization behavior, so they are not rows; they are summarized under fits_no_version. Adam's reported accuracy is a single-seed optimizer comparison in Section 7.2 and is not an independently evaluated claim-version result; cited comparisons are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local-connectivity explanations.

Systematic learning-rate and decay tuning; broader tuning; training-performance parity; decoupled weight decay; a standard training-time Adam-to-SGD switch; language benchmarks; robustness across seeds.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large batches.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Add the direct Adam-versus-SGD comparison: Adam 93.68% versus constant-momentum SGD 95.51% best test accuracy, ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, 200 epochs, seed 42. Adam uses learning rate 0.001 with cosine decay to 0.00001 and weight decay 0.0005. Its single-seed status limits confidence but does not justify excluding its own measured result from V4.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats global momentum scheduling as evidence about adaptive optimizers. A training/test-gap measurement is not required for V4's held-out-performance comparison. Although rows_left_out explicitly declares the Adam omission, its rationale is incorrect; the missing entry identifies the comparison needed to repair the record. Table 15's error counts do not consistently correspond to its best accuracies and should not be converted into best-checkpoint accuracy values.

rows.subject: Baseline (µ = 0.9)
rows.operation_detail: Train with constant momentum under the 200-epoch cosine learning-rate schedule.

conditions.value: random crop and random horizontal flip

rows.measure: Best test accuracy; epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.note: Reference condition for the physics schedule; it does not itself compare training and test error.
rows.check: This is the reference for momentum-schedule experiments, not the SGD comparator in the Adam experiment. The relevant SGD accuracy in Table 15 is 95.51%.

rows.subject: Physics (µ = 1 − 2√α)
rows.operation_detail: Train with critical-damping momentum clamped to [0.5, 0.99] under the 200-epoch cosine learning-rate schedule.

conditions.value: random crop and random horizontal flip

rows.measure: Best test accuracy; epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: mean ± std; n = 5; accuracy difference −0.46 pp, paired t-test p = 0.009; speedup 2.34×, one-sided paired t-test p = 4 × 10−4
rows.note: Faster to 90% but lower final test accuracy than baseline. The paper explicitly calls the accuracy deficit real and systematic.
rows.check: Compares two SGD momentum schedules; neither is an adaptive optimizer of the kind V4 names. The accuracy and milestone values are correctly extracted.

rows.subject: 1cycle (Smith)

conditions.value: random crop and random horizontal flip

rows.measure: Best test accuracy; epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.note: The paper reports the values but does not characterize this small difference as a generalization effect.
rows.check: A scheduled global momentum coefficient does not constitute the adaptive-optimizer comparison named in V4.

rows.subject: Baseline (µ = 0.9), T = 60

rows.subject: Hybrid-90
rows.operation_detail: Use critical-damping momentum until test accuracy reaches 90%, then switch to µ = 0.9.
rows.measure: Best test accuracy; epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.note: The authors call final accuracy indistinguishable from baseline while reporting 2.4× faster progress to 90%; this is a schedule comparison, not a direct training/test error gap measurement.
rows.check: Switches between SGD momentum schedules, not from Adam to SGD. The switch uses test accuracy, so the test set also controls training.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, 200 epochs, seed 42, the fixed optimizer recipes in Section 7.1
relationships.reason: Table 15 reports Adam best test accuracy of 93.68% versus 95.51% for constant-momentum SGD, a 1.83 percentage-point deficit. This verdict rests on the text; no extracted row captures that comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Reported best test accuracy is 93.68% for Adam versus 95.51% for constant-momentum SGD, but this single-seed comparison remains unverified.
